text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-01: I re-read app.js:1048-1103 and index.html:296/316 directly. The comment at app.js:1048 is verbatim '// --- Chart.js Benchmark Simulation ---'; lines 1053-1055 map AF3_CANDIDATES[].code/.cei/Math.abs(.dg) straight into the chart; the literals are declared at app.js:125-134. Confirmed. I re-ran the reviewer's word-boundary greps myself with `grep -owiE` over all four files: baseline, held-out, holdout, 'test set', validation, cross-validation, k-fold, ablation, 'error bar', 'confidence interval', p-value, 'sample size', scrambled, scramble, control, bootstrap, significance, Bonferroni, FDR, AUROC, enrichment, RMSD, TM-score, DockQ, ECE, calibration, PoseBusters, CASP, CAMEO all return exactly 0. Confirmed. CEI: grep for 'CEI|Cognitive Enhancement' returns only app.js:1063 (a chart label), index.html:306 (a column header) and index.html:316 (a panel title) -- no definition, no formula, no units anywhere. Confirmed. I recomputed Pearson r(CEI,|dG|) = 0.9389 -- the reviewer's 0.939 is exact. Ordering: pLDDT has 4 descending inversions, |dG| has 3 (positions 4-5, 7-8, 9-10, exactly as stated), CEI has 1. Correction: The reviewer's ordering argument overstates. CEI has exactly ONE inversion (rank 3 = 92.1 below rank 4 = 93.8) and r(rank, CEI) = -0.9845; nine of ten positions are reproduced by a plain descending-CEI sort. The evident sort key is descending CEI with a single transposition of rows 3 and 4, not, as the reviewer writes, an ordering in which 'the ordering has no rule' and where 'No composite of the three columns reproduces the ordering either.' That phrasing invites an easy rebuttal and it changes the fix: the action is to publish CEI's definition and repair one transcription error, not to invent a scoring function from scratch. Second, minor: the reviewer attributes raw substring hits for 'control' to the OrbitControls variable. Whole-word 'control' is indeed 0, but whole-word 'controls' occurs 8 times (app.js:406, 930-932, 953, 1032 twice; index.html:16, 276) as the Three.js variable -- the parenthetical is right in substance but the grep as described would not have produced it. Neither correction touches the finding's conclusion: there is no benchmark, no baseline, no held-out data, and CEI is undefined. One wrinkle in the fix worth flagging to whoever implements it: fix item (3) says to run the 25 sequences 'plus a matched set of baselines ... through the same pipeline', but there is no pipeline to run them through, and a small-molecule positive control such as donepezil does not yield a score commensurable with a peptide binder's ipTM, so the four arms cannot literally share one axis.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-02: I reimplemented app.js:787-794, :844-851 and :711-755 in Python and ran them over the actual 25 sequences. Every headline number is exact. Total residues 876 (reviewer: 876). Plotted pLDDT range [89.0, 99.0] (reviewer: exactly [89.0, 99.0]). Clamp at app.js:792 (>100) never fires; clamp at app.js:793 (<70) never fires -- both dead, confirmed. Band split: 67 of 876 residues (7.65%) in [89.0, 90.0), 92.35% above 90 -- the reviewer's 7.6%/92.4% is exact; bands 'Low (50-70)' and 'Very Low (<50)' at index.html:390-391 receive 0 residues and are structurally unreachable. Period 2*pi/0.4 = 15.708 confirmed. ASCII mod-5 buckets verified residue by residue: {A,F,K,P}=0, {G,L,Q,V}=1, {C,H,M,R,W}=2, {D,I,N,S}=3, {E,T,Y}=4 -- the reviewer's partition is exactly right; P and A do collide, G and L do collide. PAE ceiling 44*0.4+0.9 = 18.5 against an axis captioned '0 - 30 Angstrom' at index.html:397, so 38.3% of the advertised range is unreachable; reviewer's 38% confirmed. Spheres: 446 drawn across the 25 modals, 111 painted non-cyan, and 104 (23.3%) painted 'High' or 'Low' at indices where the pLDDT curve in the same modal returns >= 90 -- the reviewer's 446/104/23.3% is exact. Card-vs-curve: mean absolute discrepancy 1.051, max 2.693 at id 3 (card 97.0 at app.js:166 vs drawn mean 94.31) -- reviewer's 1.05 / 2.69 / id 3 / 97.0 / 94.31 all exact. This is the most carefully verified finding in the review and I could not break any part of it. Correction: Three repairs. (1) The reviewer writes 'for the actual sequences (28-45 aa) it is 11.7-18.5 Angstrom'. Actual sequence lengths in FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA are 26-47 aa, and the per-sequence PAE maxima span 10.90-18.50 Angstrom, not 11.7-18.5. (2) '[89.0, 99.0] exactly' holds for the values actually plotted, because app.js:794 pushes score.toFixed(1); the unrounded function cannot attain the endpoints since sin(0.4i) never equals plus or minus 1 at integer i. State it as the plotted range so an author cannot quibble; the dead-clamp conclusion is unaffected. (3) Two further defects in the same panels are missed and strengthen the finding: app.js:844 caps the PAE grid at 45, but id 1's sequence is 47 aa, so its heatmap silently drops residues 46-47 while captioned as that candidate's matrix; and because `error` at app.js:850 depends on i but not j, the matrix is not symmetric -- 1,484 of 2,025 cells in id 1's map disagree with their transpose.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on AIML-03: I parsed all 25 sequence fields programmatically rather than trusting the quotation. Exactly four sequences appear twice and every reported metric matches the reviewer character for character: KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG at app.js:153 (id 2: -16.2, 2.1 nM, 94.8) and app.js:247 (id 11: -17.5, 0.65 nM, 94.3); CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH at app.js:173 (id 4: -16.9, 1.2 nM, 95.1, Frizzled-8 CRD) and app.js:371 (id 23: -16.1, 2.8 nM, 93.8, ZO-1/Occludin); SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC at app.js:195 (id 6: -16.5, 1.8 nM, 93.2, alpha7 nAChR ECD) and app.js:319 (id 18: -15.7, 3.8 nM, 92.8, TLR4/MD-2); VRACPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH at app.js:205 (id 7: -17.2, 0.85 nM, 95.8, TrkB D5) and app.js:361 (id 22: -15.8, 3.6 nM, 94.1, EAAT2/GLT-1). Thermodynamics re-derived independently: RT at 298.15 K = 0.592484 kcal/mol; id 1's Kd of 0.32 nM implies dG = -12.9533 against a reported -18.4, so the reviewer's -12.95 is exact. Across all 25 the residual is mean -4.735, SD 0.546, spanning 3.85 to 5.73 kcal/mol, and the reported dG is more negative than implied in 25 of 25 cases -- the reviewer's '-4.74 +/- 0.55' and '3.85 to 5.73' are exact, and the 1.9 kcal/mol spread does rule out a single fixed reference-state or unit-convention offset. Alphabet: ids 4 and 23 contain B; id 24's sequence field at app.js:381 is the literal string 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate' carrying 19 distinct non-standard characters and still assigned pLDDT 92.4 at app.js:384. All confirmed; I could not refute any element. Correction: The reviewer materially UNDERSTATES the effect. Cross-referencing FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA against AF3_CANDIDATES yields seven further byte-identical collisions carrying a THIRD divergent metric set: KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFEELWKKLAEKYFELLKKYG is also AF3 rank 7 (app.js:131, pLDDT 92.8, dG -12.6), so one identical string carries pLDDT 94.8 / 94.3 / 92.8 and dG -16.2 / -17.5 / -12.6; SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCACYPGWLGCDERACPRCHGFWREVC is also AF3 rank 10 (app.js:134, 90.7, -12.1); and AF3 ranks 3, 8 and 9 (app.js:127, 132, 133) are byte-identical to ids 3, 8 and 9 with different pLDDT and dG in each case. The true spread on a single identical input is 2.5 pLDDT units and 4.9 kcal/mol -- three to six times the '0.4-1.7 units' and '0.8-1.4 kcal/mol' reported. Additionally AF3_CANDIDATES rank 6 (app.js:130) also contains B and is the string rendered to users at index.html:291 under the caption 'FASTA Sequence (AlphaFold3 Design)'; the alphabet finding is scoped to the 25 only and misses it.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-04: Verified directly. All 25 `affinity` fields (app.js:146, 156, 166, 176, 186, 198, 208, 218, 228, 238, 250, 260, 270, 280, 290, 302, 312, 322, 332, 342, 354, 364, 374, 384, 394) report only dG, Kd and a monomer pLDDT. AF3_CANDIDATES (app.js:125-134) carries plddt, dg and cei and no iptm/ptm/pae_interaction. Leaderboard columns at index.html:303-307 are Rank / Code / Target / pLDDT / dG / CEI. Word-boundary grep for ipTM, pTM and DockQ returns 0 in all four files. I searched for UniProt-style accessions, PDB IDs in a PDB context, ChEMBL ids and Ensembl ids across README.md, app.js and index.html: zero hits. There is genuinely no target structure and no accession anywhere, so no complex can have been predicted, and the core claim -- a binding assertion supported only by a monomer confidence metric, with no scrambled negative, no literature positive, no decoy panel and no self-consistency loop -- stands. 'decoy' occurs exactly 5 times (README:62, 82, 85; app.js:161; index.html:230), all as compound names, never as a control set; the reviewer's count is exact. Correction: Two corrections, one of which strengthens the finding. (1) The reviewer states 'grep for ipTM/iPTM/pTM/DockQ/interface returns zero hits across all four files.' That is false for 'interface': app.js:126 contains 'TrkB Dimerization Interface' as the target string for AF3 rank 2. The hit is a target label rather than an interface metric, so the substantive claim survives, but an author can rebut the review with one grep and the sentence must be corrected before issue. (2) The reviewer frames this as 'the wrong metric class for the claim.' The sharper and unanswerable statement, never made, is that AlphaFold3 emits no binding free energy and no dissociation constant in any configuration -- it returns coordinates plus pLDDT, PAE, pTM and ipTM. Two of the three quantities on every affinity line are therefore not AF3 outputs at all, independent of whether a complex was predicted; that should lead the finding. (3) Overstatement to trim: the reviewer says the duplicate pairs 'measure' a specificity margin 'at roughly 0.8-1.4 kcal/mol.' Nothing was measured -- no target was ever supplied to any procedure. Phrase it as 'the same string carries two different asserted affinities against unrelated targets'; calling it a measured margin concedes the premise the review is attacking.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-05: Every cited location verified by line number. README:60 (+280% LTP), :64 (+310% spine density), :67 (+240% working memory), :71 ('2x' processing speed), :74 (+350% ACh), :84 (+420% Abeta degradation), :88 (+45% CBF) all read as quoted; a regex sweep of README.md returns exactly the set {+280%, +310%, +240%, +350%, +420%, +45%} and nothing else, so the enumeration is complete. Impossible-as-estimates values confirmed at app.js:147 ('0% Cardiotoxicity'), :157 ('Tolerance Rate: 0.0%'), :209 ('Off-target Binding: None'), :251 ('Peripheral Side Effects: None'), :281 ('Fibril Blockade: 100%'), :323 ('Cytokine Storm Risk: 0%'), :375 ('BBB Disruption Risk: 0.0%'), plus composite scores at :291, :343, :395. Zero-variance predictor claim verified exactly: the hERG substring is 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM' identically in 24 of 25 entries and 'hERG IC50 > 50 uM (0% Cardiotoxicity)' in the 25th -- precisely '24 exactly, 1 with an appended'. Seizure Index distribution counted: 0.00 nine times, 0.01 eight times, 0.02 four times, absent four times -- exact. Word-boundary grep for 'sample size', 'confidence interval', 'p-value', 'bootstrap', 'Bonferroni' and 'FDR' returns 0 across all files. The 'LTP +280% has no referent' argument is correct and is a legitimate operational-definition claim well within scope: the field convention is percent-of-baseline fEPSP slope, the README fixes no comparator, so the number cannot be falsified. Correction: One quantitative slip. The reviewer writes 'log2(3) is approximately 1.58 bits of total information for a 25-compound safety screen.' log2 of the symbol count is not the information content: the empirical Shannon entropy of the observed 9/8/4 distribution is 1.510 bits per compound, and the total over the 21 populated entries is about 31.7 bits, not 1.58. Say 'at most 1.58 bits per compound, empirically 1.51', or drop the bit count and keep the plain observation that three distinct values across 25 chemically distinct entities cannot support a validation. Second, an omission in the fix rather than the finding: README:98 reads 'All 25 candidates underwent rigorous computational safety screening' -- an affirmative assertion that a procedure was executed, categorically different from an unsupported point estimate and the single sentence that most directly misrepresents what was done. It appears in no evidence_location and 'Rewrite Section 3' does not name it; it must be deleted explicitly.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on AIML-06: Verified against the repository itself. `git ls-files` returns 235 tracked paths, overwhelmingly under .agents/skills/**; there is no structures/, no data/, no notebook, no requirements.txt, environment.yml, package.json or Dockerfile, and no CI configuration. No mmCIF, PDB or confidences JSON exists anywhere in the tree, so 'designed via AlphaFold3' has zero corresponding artifact. My accession sweep (UniProt pattern, ChEMBL, Ensembl, PDB-in-context) across README.md, app.js and index.html returned zero, so residue-numbering claims such as app.js:144 ('TrkB Ig-like D5 Domain (Asp298, Glu319, Tyr342, Val312, Leu333)') and app.js:164 ('Keap1 Kelch Domain (Tyr334, Arg415, Arg483, Ser602)') are genuinely uncheckable against any numbering convention -- in my judgement the most insidious item in the whole review, and correctly identified. Dependency pinning verified: index.html:18 loads 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js' with no version, while index.html:15 pins three.js r128, :16 pins OrbitControls to 0.128.0 and :13 pins Font Awesome 6.4.0 -- the reviewer's split assessment is accurate. The unused-tooling point is verified and is the strongest rhetorical element: .agents/skills/ does contain pdb-database, uniprot-database, chembl-database (with chembl_api.py) and alphafold-database-fetch-and-analyze containing scripts/analyze_plddt.py and scripts/analyze_pae.py -- literally the two quantities app.js:791 and :850 fabricate. Correction: The grep sentence is imprecise. 'Word-boundary grep for seed, provenance, version, PDB, UniProt, DOI across the four files returns zero relevant hits' -- 'seed' returns 1 (README:77, 'Toxic Abeta-AChE seed blockade', biological seeding) and 'PDB' returns 1 (index.html:359, 'live 3D prediction and PDB/CIF download'). The hedge 'relevant' saves the claim since neither is a provenance record, but the raw counts are not zero and the sentence should say so rather than lean on the hedge. Also add to the missing-artifact inventory: the repository carries a 'License: Private Research' badge at README:4 but no LICENSE file, and no CITATION.cff.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on AIML-07: Fully verified with no material error. index.html:42 is an anchor to https://alphafoldserver.com/ whose visible text is 'AlphaFold Server Live Connected'; it carries no state, performs no probe, and would read identically offline. README:24 says 'direct live integration with the official AlphaFold Server'; README:111 says 'Live AlphaFold Server Connection'; index.html:358 says 'AlphaFold Server Live 3D Pipeline'; index.html:363 is a second plain anchor to the same homepage; app.js:660-671 is navigator.clipboard.writeText and nothing else. I independently grepped app.js, index.html, README.md and styles.css for fetch, XMLHttpRequest, axios, WebSocket, EventSource and sendBeacon: all six return exactly 0. No network request of any kind is issued, so nothing displayed can originate from AlphaFold Server. The clipboard trap is real: copyModalFasta performs no validation, so ids 4 and 23 (containing B) and id 24 (the English string) go to the clipboard for submission to a service that rejects both. Branding verified: README:3 is a shields.io badge with logo=google reading 'AlphaFold3 - DeepMind_Server', and index.html:30 reads 'DeepMind Structural Pharmacology & AlphaFold3 De Novo Platform'. Correction: The inventory of false-provenance strings is incomplete. index.html:410 (footer) reads 'Generated with AlphaFold3 3D Structural Modeling & Structural Pharmacology Algorithms', and index.html:6-7 (title tag and meta description) assert 'AlphaFold3 de novo engineered candidates' -- three further locations absent from the reviewer's list, all of which must be corrected alongside index.html:42 and README:24/111 or the relabelling will be partial. Separately, I would lift the DeepMind-branding sub-point out of why_it_matters into its own bullet in the required fix: the working directory is named DeepMind_Bio, the header claims DeepMind, and the README badge carries Google's logo. That is a third-party trademark and implied-affiliation problem distinct from a mislabelled UI control, and it is the one item in this review with external legal consequence if the repository is ever made public. The finding's MAJOR severity is still right.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: AlphaFold3 emits no binding free energy and no Kd, in any configuration -- never stated, and it is the cleanest single disproof available. AF3 returns coordinates plus pLDDT, PAE, pTM and ipTM (Abramson et al., Nature 2024, 630(8016):493-500, DOI 10.1038/s41586-024-07487-w; I confirmed volume, issue and pages via PubMed PMID 38718835). Two of the three quantities on every one of the 25 affinity lines (app.js:146 et seq., 'dG = ... | Kd = ... | AF3 pLDDT = ...') therefore cannot be AF3 outputs regardless of whether a complex was predicted. AIML-04 reaches the right conclusion by the longer monomer-vs-interface route and leaves the shorter one unused.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: 'Designed via AlphaFold3' names a predictor as a designer, and no generative procedure is described anywhere. AF3 does not produce sequences. Neither the review nor any of its seven fixes asks what method generated the 25 strings. The answer is visible in the data: the sequences are recombinations of a small reused motif pool -- id 8 (app.js:215) is GCPWECDRRACPCYRGFWR + ERACPDCH + SEAEFRLFRDVWANYCAC, and all three fragments appear separately in ids 6, 16 and 21. That is string concatenation, not design, and it is directly checkable. Any remediation plan must demand a stated design method before it demands evaluation of that method's output.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: 'TOP 10' has no denominator -- the most elementary evaluation-design defect in the artifact, and neither AIML-01 nor AIML-04 names it. index.html:265 and README:130 present an 'AlphaFold3 De Novo Engineered Candidates TOP 10' and a leaderboard, but the ten AF3_CANDIDATES codes are disjoint from the 25 drug codes, so no candidate population is ever stated from which a top ten was selected. A selection claim without a population is unevaluable in principle: no denominator, no selection rule, no report of what was discarded. Fixing the sort key does not touch this.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: No task definition and no falsification criterion. The review correctly enumerates what is procedurally missing (split, baseline, dispersion) but never observes that the artifact states no task, no success criterion, and no decision the numbers are meant to support. Without that, AIML-01 fixes (3) and (4) have nothing to be evaluated against -- one cannot construct a held-out set for an unspecified prediction problem. Remediation order should be: state the task and the decision, then the metric, then the split, then the controls.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: The reviewer's engineering praise is wrong on its main example, which weakens the report where it can least afford it. 'The Three.js scene lifecycle ... competently written' is incorrect: initModal3DCanvas allocates a new THREE.WebGLRenderer at app.js:688 on every modal open; `dispose` appears nowhere in app.js (grep returns zero); closeDrugModal (app.js:655-658) only toggles a CSS class; and the guard at app.js:764 tests the module-level modalThreeRenderer, which is reassigned but never nulled, so every previously started requestAnimationFrame loop keeps running and each applies rotation.y += 0.006 at app.js:767 to the current global mesh group. Opening N drug modals leaks N WebGL contexts (browsers cap at roughly 16, after which the panel blanks) and spins the model N times faster. Only the Chart.js teardown at app.js:779-781 deserves the praise given.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: Two further defects inside the PAE panel, both checkable in seconds. app.js:844 caps the grid at min(length, 45), but id 1's sequence is 47 aa, so its heatmap silently omits two residues while captioned as that candidate's matrix. And because `error` at app.js:850 depends on i but not j, the matrix is not symmetric: 1,484 of 2,025 cells in id 1's map disagree with their transpose. It is not merely a wrong PAE map; it is not a well-formed PAE object.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: A distributional argument that covers the 21 non-duplicated rows, which the exact-duplicate proof cannot reach. All 25 Kd values fall in 0.08-4.8 nM, all 25 dG in -15.2 to -19.5 kcal/mol, and the dG-vs-Kd residual varies by only 1.88 kcal/mol (SD 0.546) across the whole set. Twenty-five independent predictions landing inside a 4.3 kcal/mol window with no outlier, no failure and no null is itself quantitative evidence of authorship rather than computation. AIML-05 gestures at 'uniform positivity' qualitatively; stated as a distributional test it applies to every row, including those with no duplicate to contradict them.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: On citations, for the record rather than as a criticism: I resolved all eleven independently and every one is real with the stated title, venue, volume and pages. Abramson 2024 Nature 630(8016):493-500 and Pacesa 2025 Nature 646(8084):483-492 confirmed via PubMed (PMID 38718835, 40866699); Buttenschoen/Morris/Deane Chem Sci 2024 15(9):3130-3139, Simpkin Proteins 2023 91:1616-1635 and Robin Proteins 2021 89:1977-1986 via Crossref; the two 2025 openRxiv preprints (10.1101/2025.08.14.670059, 10.1101/2025.08.15.670450) and the ADMET audit under the unfamiliar 10.64898 prefix (which is openRxiv's, not a fabrication) all resolve with exact titles; arXiv 2507.21404, 2102.09548 and 1706.04599 confirmed. I also checked the two specific LIT-PCBA figures the reviewer quotes and both are verbatim from the abstract: 323 active train-validation analogue pairs at ECFP4 Tanimoto >= 0.6 in ALDH1, and 2,491 2D-identical inactives spanning partitions. The citation record is clean and the review may be issued on that basis.
